brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three full-depth hex bases in a straight row (piece:-1,0,0, piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0), joined and locked with joint bolts, with solid end caps on every open face. It is a wall-mountable block, but I did not verify the wall-facing orientation against a real wall; the keyhole hangers face one side of the row.
Three hex-bin-full-div2 bins (2-compartment full-depth trays) at cells -1,0; 0,0; 1,0 (bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0).
Three hex-acc-keyhole accessories, one on each base (accessory:0#-1,0#1, accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#1,0#1), on the same face slot. check_build reports no errors and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell spice rack: a row of three full hex bases, each holding a two-compartment bin and a keyhole hanger on the same face, joined with joint bolts and capped on open faces. check_build is clean (meshClash clear). Not verified: material strength, the actual screw spacing on a wall, and whether the keyhole face points exactly at the wall you choose. No spice-jar props were added.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
